description: Planned Mitiq-backed zero-noise extrapolation wrapper for noisy quantum evolution circuits. This is not a standalone evolution method; it post-processes results from an evolution circuit executed on a noisy simulator or hardware backend.
applicable_hamiltonians: Any Hamiltonian whose evolution circuit can be executed on a Mitiq-compatible backend
Trotterized or other circuit-based evolution methods
limitations: Not a state evolution strategy by itself; requires a base evolution method and executor
Requires repeated circuit executions at multiple noise scale factors
Improves noise-affected observables statistically but does not remove algorithmic approximation error
Effectiveness depends on the backend noise model, observable, shot budget, and extrapolation fit

base_method.description: Evolution method used to generate the base circuit or observable workflow.

scale_factors.description: Noise scale factors used for zero-noise extrapolation.

factory.description: Extrapolation model, such as linear, polynomial, or exponential.

shots.description: Number of shots per scaled circuit execution.

backend_requirements: noisy simulator or quantum hardware executor
execution.non_executable_reason: No registered OpenQEvo method or adapter currently implements mitiq_zne.

complexity.gate_count: N/A as a post-processing wrapper; circuit executions are multiplied by the number of noise scale factors
complexity.circuit_depth: Depends on the base evolution circuit and noise-scaling strategy
complexity.error_scaling: Mitigates stochastic hardware or simulator noise in measured observables; does not change base method algorithmic error scaling

references.title: Mitiq: A software package for error mitigation on noisy quantum computers
